The bottom panel prints specific results (94.3%, 90.6%, 3.7 pt gap, p = 9.9x10^-20) that never appear in that form in the body text, so a reader cannot connect them to a table. 'ASR Transcript (Whisper)' does not say which Whisper checkpoint.
findings.evidence: Figure 1 bottom panel: 'Reference (Correct) 94.3% / ASR (Whisper) 90.6% / Accuracy Gap = 3.7 percentage points'; 'McNemar's exact test... p = 9.9 x 10^-20'; Stage 2 box labeled 'Llama-3.1-8B'.
findings.suggested_fix: Simplify the figure (drop the full MCQ text or enlarge it), label the ASR system as Whisper-M, and state the pooled 94.3%/90.6% numbers in the QA results text with a pointer to Table 3.

findings.title: Figures 2 and 3: unstated data pooling, tiny rotated labels
findings.location: Figure 2 and Figure 3 with captions (page 5, left column)
findings.description: Figure 2's caption does not say whether WER is pooled over EdX and M3AV or over which recordings (the values are consistent with a 25/75 L1/L2 pooled Whisper-M WER of 0.074, but this must be stated). Figure 3's value labels are rotated 90 degrees in very small type and the x-axis tick labels are long and rotated 30 degrees, leaving the plot area small.
findings.evidence: Figure 2 caption: 'ASR performance over speaker group (L1 vs. L2) measured by WER.' Figure 3 labels such as '0.054', '0.081', '0.072' are approximately 3pt and rotated.
findings.suggested_fix: State the pooling in both captions; enlarge labels or move exact values into a table in the appendix/main text.

findings.title: Table 4 mixes proportions and percentage points; open-ended McNemar 'n=173' unexplained
findings.location: Table 4 and caption (page 6); text 'toward=140, away=33, n=173'
findings.description: ref/asr are given as proportions (0.803, 0.700) while 'drop' is in 'pt' (10.3pt), and the caption's parenthetical '(ref vs. Whisper-M ASR transcript)' is awkwardly placed. The text samples '300 questions' but reports a test with n=173; n presumably counts discordant pairs pooled over three LLMs (from 900 comparisons), which is not stated.
findings.evidence: Caption: 'QA accuracy over open-ended questions with (ref vs. Whisper-M ASR transcript) and Cohen's h.' Rows: 'GPT4o 0.803 0.700 10.3pt 0.240'. Text: 'we randomly sample 300 questions' ... '(toward=140, away=33, n=173, p = 3.4 x 10^-17)'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use percentages throughout the table, reword the caption, and define n as the number of discordant (question, model) pairs.

findings.title: Reference list formatting: 'et al.' in author fields, missing venues/pages, capitalization
findings.location: References, pages 8-9
findings.description: Several entries truncate authors with 'et al.' contrary to AAAI style (Chen 2024; Dubey 2024; Kwon 2023; Zheng 2023). Hollands, Blackburn, and Christensen 2022 has no venue at all. (The split words 'Y ang', 'T utoring', 'P .' seen in text extraction are kerning artifacts and do not appear in the rendered PDF; the list is otherwise complete and not truncated.)

Evaluating the performance of state-of-the-art ASR systems on non-native English using corpora with extensive language background variation.' (no venue); 'Zhao, R.; ... 2025. Learnlens: Llm-enabled personalised'.
findings.suggested_fix: List full author lists, add venues/pages/article numbers, and fix capitalization in the .bib entries.

findings.title: Which Whisper decoding setting for EdX is reported?
findings.location: Page 3, 'ASR Transcription and Error Analysis', first paragraph
findings.description: Whisper models are said to be 'additionally run' with language fixed to English on EdX, implying both auto-detect and fixed-English runs exist. The results never say which run populates Table 2, Figure 2, Figure 3 and the QA experiments.
findings.evidence: 'For EdX, Whisper models are additionally run with decoding language fixed to English (language="en") rather than automatic language detection, following an observed accuracy improvement ...; M3AV transcription fixes English decoding throughout.'
findings.suggested_fix: State which configuration is reported and, if both were run, report the size of the observed improvement.

findings.title: How does '228 candidate NIH speakers' relate to 123 M3AV videos?
findings.location: Page 3 col. 1 (L1/L2 status paragraph); Table 1
findings.description: The text says 16 of 228 candidate NIH speakers were excluded for unresolvable background, yet the entire M3AV subset used is 123 videos across three venues (Table 1). The candidate pool, the selection step from 228 to the final set, and whether 'speakers' equals 'videos' are not explained.
findings.evidence: 'speakers whose background could not be resolved this way are coded as unknown and excluded from the selected set (e.g., 16 of 228 candidate NIH speakers)'; Table 1: 'M3AV 123 3 venues 3 31 92'.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the M3AV sampling procedure (candidate pool, selection criteria, final counts per venue) in one or two sentences.

findings.title: Hallucination/repetition explanation for Whisper-L is asserted without evidence
findings.location: Page 5, 'ASR Errors Across Speakers and Domains', first paragraph
findings.description: The counter-intuitive finding that Whisper-L (WER 0.197) is far worse than Whisper-S (0.075) is attributed to hallucination and repetition on long audio 'rather than a genuine capability deficit', but no count, example, or insertion-rate statistic is given, and Table 2 does not break WER into S/D/I even though page 3 says errors are so categorized.
findings.evidence: 'Inspection of individual transcripts shows this is driven by hallucination and repetition failures on long lecture audio rather than a genuine capability deficit.' Table 2 reports only CER/WER/BWER.
findings.suggested_fix: Report insertion rates or the fraction of segments with repetition loops per system, or include an example transcript excerpt.
